subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group user isolation be implemented as automatic group-scoped dynamic agents/subagents, as generic channel/session SDK behavior, or deferred to narrower existing issues?
rationale: Current source shows adjacent session and thread-binding mechanisms, but the requested automatic group subagent lifecycle crosses product, security, resource-management, memory, and plugin/core boundary choices that cannot be inferred from existing behavior.

options.title: Design Feishu/channel contract first
options.body: Keep this open for a maintainer-owned design that defines lifecycle, authorization, quota, memory, routing, and skill/config policy before code is queued.

options.title: Limit to current session model
options.body: Declare `groupSessionScope` plus explicit subagent/thread bindings as the supported model and route the broader per-user assistant workflow to narrower follow-ups.

options.title: Prototype outside core first
options.body: Ask for an external Feishu/channel plugin experiment that proves the lifecycle and security model before expanding bundled plugin or SDK contracts.

recommendation.title: Design Feishu/channel contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this open for a maintainer-owned design that defines lifecycle, authorization, quota, memory, routing, and skill/config policy before code is queued.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a Feishu plugin product/security decision, and the plugin metadata names this handle as the Feishu/Lark community maintainer.
